questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses and academic opportunities, possibility for creating social network and the destination to be economical accessible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I assume 10 being the best in the above question.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy: The host university had a great introductional 'webinar' before arrival with a lot of useful information on e.g. public transport, necessary apps for the university and city, cultural differences, etc. Furthermore, the host university had a monthly newsletter with additional information on special events in the area and important deadlines on the university. Upon arrival a very detailed information sheet was send by the host university. Overall, I found myself to be informed upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When arrived at my study destination, a short welcome/introduction meeting was held at the university, where further information was given. Including how to find one's class room and making sure that our student ID was ready, etc. I have not sought any specific assistance out - just attended the scheduled meetings, where I found to find all the needed information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very professional approach at my host institution and the contact persons were very helpfull and open-minded.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through the host university: I received an email with information about this co-living option (a campus-adjacent accommodation) and if I was interested in securing a room, the only thing was to write an email with some information. So it was very easy for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived at a campus-adjacent accommodation, so I only had 5-10min walk to my class room. Otherwise, I will advise future exchange students to check out where campus is located compared to housing; how much time is one to spend on transport, is it located somewhat close to potential hot-spots for student activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When choosing housing: Make a decision on whether you want to have roomies or not/ how many. I was living with 5 other exchange students, which was great in the sense that we were all new to the city, would all stay for a semester and could more easily get a network by getting to know each other. Make sure to arrange some movie nights, cooking together, etc.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received some information by email on how to navigate and how to apply for courses. Finding the specific courses relevant for me was a bit time-consuming as the semester is structured a bit differently compared to UCPH. So some courses, I would have liked to take, were not possible because of study pace and ECTS-points. Otherwise, the registration process itself was easy and not complicated: on arrival I went to the student information center and got my courses accepted through their system and got my student ID. And I was ready to attend my courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student information center at my host institution - super helpful, did most of the additional registration in their system at arrival.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Once I got to know which courses I had gotten, everything went smoothly. It was the process of finding the right courses, which was a bit time consuming and troublesome. I did not get my first priorities in courses, but the courses I ended up in were very interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded towards the courses. Some subjects might have been covered in earlier courses at your home university, but the approach and was of teaching/discussing can be very different in different countries and/or universities. And take your time with the registration process; it might take a bit longer than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took some courses at a different study program, which was very interesting. It also challenged my own academical background and understanding of my knowledge as some of the classes were critical towards medicine and public health (my own study program). So I had some really interesting discussions with my co-students and we were all international students, which meant that the cultural differences were very noticeable.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The two courses were based on a discussion-approach. We had lectures once a week and a discussion class once a week, which is less physical presence than what I have been used to at my home university. The reading amount was suitable for a 15ECTS-course and we were to write short reflection on the readings for each week. One presentation on our final paper was to be held and then the final paper was to be submitted as the exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less teaching, more discussion among us students. We did go through some of the theories and approaches but far from everything on the reading list, which I am used to at UCPH. So overall, there was more flexibility and self-study which was great in order to meet up with other students at the library, etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GS2101 Critical Studies on Gender Equality Policy and Diversity
GS2207 Body politics from feminist perspectives

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the two courses I was enrolled in - if one is interested in the subject. The flexibility enables that one can schedule different activities and makes it easier to attend e.g. ESN events. But choose courses and subjects which you find interesting - there is a greater possibility of meeting people with the same interest.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I did not pay for internet nor for laundry, all additional costs such as water, electricity, etc. was part of my housing rent. 
Many expenses were more or less the same as in CPH; I was keeping an eye on the development of the Swedish crown (SEK) - but overall it was low throughout my stay. Therefore, the expenses were lower than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not specific for the host institution, but Gothenburg is a very student friendly city! They have many discounts on different activities and if one becomes member of their "studenterkår", one will receive even more discounts and invitations to events. Through my studenterkår, I got a discount to the gym which was amazing with lots of different sport activities (bouldering, yoga, bodycombat, spinning, padl, etc.). Another university (CHALMERS) hosted a recycling-bike event were one could buy an old bike and get help to fix it for only 200SEK - and students from GU were invited as well. At my host university, events such as knitting events and informational speeches were arranged. Furthermore, there was a very strong ESN-community with many activities. My host university itself hosted some hikes and informed us exchange students on diverse things to do throughout the months in their monthly newsletter.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Knitting events, informational speeches, networking with fika. The host institution itself did not arrange that many activities but made students aware of events arranged by others. The host institution arranged an event were all student unions and different student driven clubs were presented to the exchange students. The host institution offered a free swedish class.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If possible, take part in the events hosted by ESN (Erasmus Student Network) as they plan cultural activities and fun nights - a great way to get to know other exchange students and makes it easier to settle in fast. I took a Swedish class as well, since the university offered it for free. Furthermore, make sure to do something fun - I attended a pottery class in swedish and went frequently to the gym, where I tried some new sports. Go to close-by cities and visit the archipelago. Sign up for the "Studentlistan"; you can buy very cheap last-minute-tickets to the teater and opera.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Make a trip to close-by cities such as Allingsås or Marstrand and go to Stockholm (one can find some cheap train tickets from Gothenburg!) and a must is to go to the archipelago (Skærgården) - my favorits were the southern islands. Sweden has lots of beautiful nature, so I spend many weekends on hikes. There is something called "Fritidsbanken" were one can borrow outdoor-gear for free; perfect for students!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy: Sweden and Denmark are very similar in culture. There are, however, differences which might be somewhat surprising as one tend to think that the countries are almost the same. My experience is that Sweden has a more laid-back culture; deadlines weren't taken too seriously in class or in swedish class and coming a bit late to social events was not considered rude.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It requires a greater effort to make contact with the locals from your side. Many will probably have an approach a la "you're only here for one semester, why should I invest in you", why you yourself have to be more outgoing/outreaching. It is, however, easier to socialize with local students when coming from CPH/DK. If you attend courses with international students, as I did, do some things in your spare time which allows you to meet local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The cultural differences weren't that noticeable. I was surprise of the laid-back culture at the university.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and I got to appreciate the laid-back approach.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to attend as many events/activities as possible when arriving: this is how you get to meet people. You only get to stay one semester so make sure to integrate yourself quickly in order to get the most out of your exchange.
Website: make sure to take a look at the host institution's homepage as they are announcing events and important deadlines. And don't hesitate to contact the institution if/when you have questions.
Enjoy! Time goes by fast. Eventually make a list of things you would like to know, experience, see. Ask your professors for academic events if interested - such as study programme celebrations, inspirational speeches, etc. Professors often know what happens at the faculty.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Instagram was a great source for inspiration on places to visit, flee markets, open air concerts, etc. So check it out! The host institution and the different faculties and studenterkår also have instagram profiles - make sure to follow them as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people, challenging myself in regard of having to create a network from scratch and attending events on my own, get to try new hobbies, getting to know different academical approaches and having to explain/argue in an understandable way so the audience understands your points clearly.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Attending events on my own in the beginning and very overwhelming getting to know so many people. 
And the darkness; I did not expect it to be so much more dark - and how long time it takes for spring to arrive.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: There will be ups and downs. Some days may not be very interesting, other days may be overwhelming.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
